markers.title: The branch runs before anything is decided
markers.finding: Under-age applicants were being assessed and sometimes rejected before anyone established whether a parent had agreed to any of it.
markers.decision: At sixteen, consent goes out before a single decision is recorded. The screen says so in those words, so silence does not read as rejection.
markers.rejected: Assessing first and collecting consent at the offer, which is both the wrong order legally and the wrong order for the person waiting.

markers.title: A false negative on a first job is not an acceptable error
markers.finding: The cost of wrongly rejecting a sixteen year old's first application is a person who never comes back, and the business had no way to see that happening.
markers.decision: No response at all is recorded as no decision, not as a rejection. She can return at seventeen with nothing against her name.
markers.rejected: Auto-rejecting on a consent timeout, which is the cheapest thing to build and the most expensive thing to be wrong about.

markers.title: The rate is named, in the consent
markers.finding: Parents were agreeing to employment without being told the junior rate or the hours a school night allows.
markers.decision: The rate is stated as a percentage of the adult rate, with the step-ups. A guardian agreeing to something should be able to see what it is.
markers.rejected: A link to an award summary, which is a document written for payroll and not for a parent on a phone at six in the evening.

markers.title: Age and consent are locked in the specification
markers.finding: Rules of this kind drift when a release is under time pressure, and the drift is invisible until somebody is hurt by it.
markers.decision: This branch cannot be changed without sign-off. It is written into the specification as a locked rule rather than as a default somebody can toggle.
markers.rejected: Treating it as configuration, which is how a compliance rule quietly becomes a setting.
